UI-11.answer:
The issue is that `ScreenInsets` is set to `Enum.ScreenInsets.None`, which ignores safe areas (camera notches, top status bars, Roblox UI). On phones with cutouts, this causes UI in the top-right to be hidden.

The fix is to use `Enum.ScreenInsets.DeviceSafeInsets` (or the default `CoreUISafeInsets`) so the `ScreenGui`'s coordinate space respects safe areas. Since the label is positioned using `UDim2.new(1, -150, 0, 0)` with `AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)`, it's already positioned relative to the container's bounds — which are inset when safe areas are enabled. No hard-coded pixel offsets needed.

Here's the corrected script:

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
gui.Name = "Hud"
gui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.DeviceSafeInsets  -- Respect safe areas (notches, top bar)
gui.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(140, 36)
label.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(1, 0)
label.Position = UDim2.new(1, -150, 0, 0)
label.Text = "Score: 0"
label.Parent = gui
```

**Why this works:**
- `DeviceSafeInsets` makes the `ScreenGui`'s coordinate space shrink to avoid device cutouts and the Roblox top bar [1].
- The label's position (`UDim2.new(1, -150, 0, 0)`) is already relative to the container's right edge (scale `1`), so it automatically stays within the safe area on all devices [2].
- On PC (no cutouts), `DeviceSafeInsets` has no visible effect, so the label appears at the same location as before [4].

**Citations:**
- [1] Create HUD meters > Create a screen container > Utilize safe areas — explains `ScreenInsets` and `DeviceSafeInsets`.
- [2] Create HUD meters > Construct the health meter > Position the frame — explains `UDim2` scale-based positioning.
- [4] Cross-platform development > User interface — confirms scale-based positioning works across platforms.
